q: Who's on the Ads team and what do they own?
a: Sunaina leads. Sahil owns Curly men, Wavy men, Scalp men. Saanya owns Wavy women, Curly women, Dry Shampoo. Albia owns HWS, Scalp women, HA. Sunaina personally holds OTF, Mask, HPS, Oil.

q: Who do I talk to outside the ads team?
a:
Founders Nikita & Anmol for creative direction. Rupika is the strategy/copy lead — her review carries the same weight as a founder's.

Copy team: Tania, Ryan, Nainan — scripts and captions.
Design team: Aishleen, Sehej, Mehar, Ananya, Ayushi, Sucharita, Ruchika — storyboards and edits.
Marketing: Twinkle, Cherishi, Harsh, Keshav — influencer-led campaigns and references.
Ops: Manisha — dispatch.
Finance: Tanuja — payments.

q: What are our daily and weekly rituals?
a: 11 AM standup with copy + design + ads. Weekly references call. Daily updates on email if calls don't happen. WFH must be applied for on Greythr same day.

q: What products am I selling?
a: OTF, HWS, HPS, HA, DDHM, DS, Mask, Oil; plus the Scalp / Wavy / Curly ranges, split by men and women.

q: What tools do I live in?
a: Ads tracker, Creative master, Dispatch sheet, Ads pipeline, DG frontend, Airtable. Sahil-built moxie-calculator helps with negotiation maths; moxie-agreements generates the contract. Greythr for HR/WFH. 2FA mandatory on email.

q: What does a 'good' creator look like for Moxie?
a: Four parameters articulated for the AD range: awareness, credibility, articulation, and being on-brand for Moxie. Mix beauty-credible voices (GBF, indianskinblog-archetype) with on-brand cool personas. Avoid kiddy-looking; avoid creators who can't sound credible on hi-tech formulations.

q: Where do I find creators?
a: Explore page mining is the default — Sunaina has explicitly asked the team to source 4–5 credible beauty creators from their explore pages. Add to the pipeline with portfolio assignment + IG handle in the group description so we don't lose track.

q: How do I tag a creator's archetype?
a: By delivery format (verbal, non-verbal, VO-led), by integration style (visual integration vs personal journey vs problem-solution), and by tier (>100k almost always means agency). UGC-only is its own bucket.

q: Are there creators or managers we avoid?
a: Yes — the avoid list changes over time. Ask Sunaina for the current list rather than relying on this doc. As a general note: past issues with agencies posting unauthorised content mean we are more careful with agencies going forward.

q: Should I prefer agencies or going direct?
a: Direct is preferred where possible. Agencies layer cost and have caused unauthorised-post incidents. But for >100k creators, agencies are usually unavoidable.

q: What's a 'good' rate for a creator?
a: Anchor on CPV (cost per view). CPV must be below 1 for the collab to make sense — that's the rule Sahil articulated. Pull the creator's average views and back-solve the cap.

q: What's the ceiling for emerging creators?
a: ~₹20k for emerging creators is the soft cap referenced in conversations. Push higher only for proven performers.

q: Always ask for which add-ons?
a: Always ask for perpetuity ad rights rates in addition to base. Default ad rights are 1 month (extendable). Sunaina's quote: "ad rights always get perpetuity rates — if 1 month works well we might as well run it longer."

q: What does a long-term lock-in look like?
a: Example template: 6 UGC ads in 6 months at ₹4,500 each, including 2 months of ad rights. Useful for high-fit emerging creators where you want repeat output cheaply.

q: How do I use the moxie-calculator?
a: Sahil built it. He has a deck / walkthrough ready. Sit with him before your first hard negotiation — he has explicitly offered.

q: What's the order of operations to onboard a creator?
a:
1. Negotiate.
  2. Send confirmation email.
  3. Get the agreement signed.
  4. Only then start work.

Sunaina: "boys, pls make sure they sign the agreement and then start working on their deliverables."

q: What does the confirmation email need to include?
a:
• Reference to the standard Content Creation and Collaboration Agreement (attached): "This collaboration is subject to Moxie Beauty's standard Content Creation and Collaboration Agreement, a copy of which is attached."
  • The line "10% TDS will be deducted as per government mandate" under the 100% payment-on-deliverable clause.
  • Ask the creator to reply-all with acknowledgement so creator@moxiebeauty.in is triggered.
  • CC accounts@moxiebeauty.in.

q: What if a creator pushes back on signing?
a: Friction with signing is real — Sahil flagged this. Ongoing discussion: can confirmation-of-email imply confirmation-of-agreement? Pending legal input. For now, don't start work until both email and agreement are in.

q: What format is the agreement in?
a: PDF only. Generated via the moxie-agreements tool.

q: How do I get product to a creator?
a: Add them to the dispatch sheet with the right SKU + variant — e.g., "HWS with brush", "DS with brush". Manisha runs ops.

q: The dispatch isn't triggering — why?
a: Known bug: copy-pasting an address doesn't trigger the move from sourcing → dispatch. The cell needs to register an edit. Add a . and erase it, or add a :) and remove. Workaround documented by Sahil in April '26.

q: Where does the pipeline owner show up for ops?
a: Sunaina is wiring the sourcing-tab pipeline owner into dispatch so Manisha knows who to ping for a specific delivery. If yours isn't visible, add it manually for now.

q: What's the order of creative production?
a: Copy → storyboard → design → shoot. Copy team writes script first; design picks it up; storyboard goes to creator. Standup at 11 AM aligns the pipeline daily.

q: Who writes the script?
a: Copy team — Tania, Ryan, Nainan. Only copy team has commenter access to scripts; tag the strat handle and mention Nikita or Rupika to review.

q: What does a storyboard need before it goes to a creator?
a: Approved script + frame references + lighting/setting reference + hook. Always send a test-shot ask before a full shoot.

q: Do we always need a test shot?
a: Yes — even when a creator is travelling and pushing for products. Test shot first for lighting, framing, hairstyle. Repeated rule across the chat: "told her to give us a test shot before anything is shot."

q: What 'high resolution' actually means
a: Design team's recurring complaint: creators say "high resolution" and send WhatsApp-quality video. Insist on raw / cloud upload. Reshoots are common when this is missed.

q: What does Nikita reject on sight?
a:
"Salesy." "Kiddy." "Not credible." "Not landing." "Not self-explanatory." "Not on-brand." "Lacks Moxie-ness."

If a video reads as any of those, it's a no.

q: What does Nikita value in a video?
a: Hook clarity ("hook is not clear story-wise"), strong opening shot ("zoom in more, engage better"), real hair / real results in B/A ("we should use only real hair and real results"), no abrupt edits, transitions that feel earned, lighting that doesn't make hair look "icky," product-application as the strongest hook for OTF.

q: Nikita's copy lens
a: Self-explanatory ≥ clever. She rejected "Weightless" because "it isn't self-explanatory — even on Nykaa." Likes simple, contextual lines. "Range" not "trio." Avoid wording that implies daily-use if the product isn't daily-use. Sentence-case tickers. Don't repeat the main copy in the ticker unnecessarily.

q: Nikita's visual lens
a: On-brand subtle neon. Black logo not over-covered. Hierarchy of information must be intentional. Old-fashioned PNGs okay if they help concept. Conceptual clarity beats clever visual — "not clear why propane and butane are relevant."

q: Nikita on testimonials and proof
a: "Too many product shots with clever copy. We need before-afters, testimonials, social proof, etc to complete the story." Translation: balance the asset mix.

q: What does Anmol look at first?
a: Storyline coherence and Instagram-grid feel. Asks "does this need copy on the video to set context instantly? POV: xyz." Wants snappier edits. Looks at filler shots and whether they're not outright salesy.

q: Anmol's hierarchy-of-information rule
a:
"Let's think on this from what is the hierarchy of information — too many things are grabbing attention at the same time."

If you can't articulate which element should win the user's eye in 1 second, the asset isn't done.

q: Anmol on framing
a: "This is not framed properly." Composition is non-negotiable — reshoots happen for framing alone.

q: What does Rupika check first on copy?
a:
Claim consistency — across the asset and across the brand. Examples: "we're saying 3 washes everywhere" (lock the claim once, use it everywhere) and the fix "*Instrumental results after 3 uses vs. non-conditioning shampoo and conditioner" — exact phrasing and footnote discipline.

If two claims feel like the same thing to a layperson ("stronger hair" vs "reduced breakage"), they probably need re-spacing on the asset.

q: Rupika's concept-coherence rule
a:
"The POV and the end slate aren't speaking to each other and aren't speaking to what she's shot."

Translation: opener, body, and close must tell one story. If they don't, no edit polish will save it.

q: Rupika on legitimacy — how it reads
a:
She watches whether claims look legit, not just whether they're true. Examples: bringing back the HydroRepair Complex unit on supers because "it starts making it look more legit," and asking whether the unit in neon is getting lost vs the claim itself.

Asset legitimacy = visible scientific scaffolding + readable hierarchy.

q: Rupika on tightness
a: Recurring note: "can we make this a little bit more tighter?" Length is suspicious until proven necessary. Cut intros, dedupe lines (she'll spot "haircare repeated twice at 6–7 seconds" instantly), and lose any frame that doesn't earn its place.

q: When does Rupika loop in Nikita?
a: Rupika makes the strategy/copy call first. If something is borderline, she'll explicitly say "let me check w Nikita" and come back. If you push something to Nikita without Rupika reviewing first, you've broken the queue.

q: Who approves what?
a:
Copy team writes; Rupika reviews; Nikita and Anmol approve via comments on the doc and the cut. Design final cuts go to Nikita and Anmol.

Edit feedback comes back fast and granular — "can we bring the transition sooner at 'or break'" — expect lots of small iterations.

q: When something is 'live,' what should I do?
a: Each time design + ads says something is live, check if it's your creator and send the calendar invite accordingly. Sunaina's standing instruction.

q: What's a normal shoot timeline?
a: 5–7 days from confirmation to footage in. Reshoots add another cycle. Track on the ads pipeline.

q: How do creators get paid?
a: Invoice into the system; Tanuja in finance makes payments. 10% TDS is deducted. Invoices have a form now (April '26 onwards).

q: Half-payment and extension scenarios
a: For half-payment cases: do a fresh entry and write "pay remaining half." For 1-month ad rights extensions: ask for a fresh invoice + send a calendar invite for the extension window.

q: What works and what we shouldn't experiment with
a: Sunaina's call from Feb '26: "Let's not experiment, we know what works: videos + before-and-after GIFs."

q: How do we read engagement signals?
a:
Look at who is commenting and liking. Nikita's observation: "Boys' comments are so different — nearly all the likes are also boys. Different humour. Like sometimes girls will say 'she kind of looks like the actor who plays Fleabag.' Guys will just comment 'Fleabag.'"

Useful gendered read on whether the asset is landing with the intended audience.

q: How do I learn the leadership lens fastest?
a: Read the Everything Ads thread end-to-end with the search terms: salesy, kiddy, credible, hook, self-explanatory, on-brand, tighter, legit. That's the compressed version of the taste.

q: What does my first week look like?
a:
1. Get laptop from Tanuja.
  2. 2FA on email.
  3. Greythr setup for WFH.
  4. Sit in on standup.
  5. Get assigned a portfolio.
  6. Read the agreement.
  7. Sit with Sahil for a negotiation walkthrough.

q: Things I should never do in my first month
a:
• Send a confirmation email without the agreement clause.
  • Start work before the agreement is signed.
  • Use a creator on the avoid list.
  • Ship product without putting them on the dispatch sheet.
  • Skip Rupika's review and push something straight to Nikita.
  • Approve a creative without Nikita / Anmol sign-off if it's going on a paid channel.

q: The single quickest way to embarrass yourself
a: Send leadership a creative that's "salesy," "kiddy," or "not self-explanatory." Read G1 first.
